memory_update.text: SAIL should remain a reference/control-plane identity name for machine and AI-agent governance; verify ARR expansion and non-human identity product adoption before elevating thesis strength.
TENB is a mid-cap exposure-management candidate for cloud/AI posture, identity risk, and CSPM/KSPM; key gap is whether cloud-security modules are becoming material growth drivers.
PD is a small-cap automation and incident-response control-plane candidate with direct AI-operations positioning; key gap is whether new agentic/AIOps products offset slow ARR growth.
RPD is a speculative-shadow small-cap CNAPP/cloud-security candidate; include only with explicit falsification around revenue materiality, retention, balance sheet, and competitive displacement risk.
Identity security M&A by PANW/CyberArk and ServiceNow/Veza suggests larger platforms are validating machine/AI identity and permission-governance as a strategic control-plane chokepoint.

Data lineage, secrets management, and standalone machine-identity vendors are underrepresented among US-listed small/mid caps because several pure-play assets are private or acquired; future passes should map private leaders to public acquirers and implementation partners.

node: Cloud security, identity, observability, and automation control-plane software
summary: Expanded the US-listed universe around the control-plane software chokepoint for cloud security, machine/AI identity, exposure management, CNAPP, and incident-response automation. Reference context includes larger platform consolidators such as Palo Alto Networks/CyberArk, Okta, Datadog, Dynatrace, Microsoft, and ServiceNow, but this pass prioritizes narrower public names with plausible second-order exposure and lower broad-market attention. Candidates are research leads only, not recommendations.
